# Open Eyes: full site text

> Plain-text copy of the English pages of the Open Eyes website, for language models. See llms.txt for the index.


## How to use

Source: https://your-domain.example/how-to.html

How to use Open Eyes

From a handful of shots to one photo where every face looks its best. It takes about a minute.

Before you start: take a few shots
- Take at least two photos of the same moment. Burst mode, or three or four quick taps, is ideal.
- Stay in the same spot and keep the phone at the same angle. Small movements are fine; the app lines the shots up.
- Ask everyone to hold the pose for a second. Blinks and half-smiles are exactly what the extra shots fix.
- Faces work best when they look roughly toward the camera and aren't covered by hands, hair or glasses glare.


### Step 1
Choose your shots
Open Open Eyes and tap Choose Photos to Fix. Pick 2 to 9 shots of the same moment from your gallery. The app only sees the photos you pick.


### Step 2
Pick your favorite
Tap the shot you like best overall: the framing, the light, the expressions you're happy with. This is the photo you'll keep; the other shots lend it their eyes and smiles.
Changed your mind later? Go back and pick a different favorite.


### Step 3
Let it look at your shots
Open Eyes finds the faces, lines up your shots and matches each face across them. You'll see Finding faces…, Lining up your shots… and Matching faces across shots…. Everything stays on your phone.


### Step 4
Tap a face to fix it
Faces another shot can improve have a yellow ring and a sparkle. The line under the photo tells you how many.
- Tap a highlighted face, then Use the best shots to take the suggested eyes and smile in one go.
- Or choose yourself: under Eyes and Smile, tap a shot. The one marked Best is the app's suggestion; As is keeps your favorite's own face.
- Undo steps back for that face. Tap Done to close.

Fixed faces turn green with a check. When nothing is left to improve you'll see Looking good. Tap Save copy when you're done.


### Step 5
Save a copy
Tap Save copy. Your fixed photo is saved to your gallery as a new photo (on Android in Pictures/Open Eyes, on iPhone in your Photos library). The original shots are untouched.
The share sheet opens right away if you want to send it.


### Step 6
Come back to it later
Your fixes are listed under Recent fixes on the home screen. Tap one to change it again; the app reopens your shots and restores your choices. Removing a fix from the list doesn't delete the photo from your gallery.

If something doesn't work

“No faces were found in your favorite shot”

Tap Pick a different favorite and try another shot, or start over with a sharper set. Very small, blurry or sideways faces may not be found.

“This face isn't clear enough in your other shots”

That person is hidden, turned away or missing in the other shots, so there's nothing to take from them. Their face stays as it is in your favorite.

A fix doesn't look right

Pick another shot for that face, or tap Undo. Fixes look best when the head is in a similar position in both shots; a hand in front of the face comes along with the fix.

“One of the shots this fix was made from has been deleted”

The fix can't be changed any more because a source shot is gone. The fixed photo is still in your gallery.

Still stuck? Contact support.


## Questions and answers

Source: https://your-domain.example/faq.html

Questions and answers

Can't find your question? Ask us.

Is this an AI photo app?
No pixels are generated. Every eye and smile in a fixed photo comes from another shot you took. The app uses on-device face detection only to find where the eyes and mouth are, then lines up and blends the real pixels. That's why fixed photos are labelled as a composite, not as AI-generated. More about labels.

Are my photos uploaded anywhere?
No. Your photos and face data never leave your phone. There's no account and no cloud processing. See the privacy policy for the details.

Does it work with just one person?
Yes. Portraits, selfies and groups all work the same way: as long as there are at least two shots of the same moment.

How many photos can I use?
Between 2 and 9 shots of the same moment. More shots give the app more chances to find open eyes and a good smile.

Will my original photos be changed?
Never. Each fix is saved as a new photo. Your original shots stay exactly as they were.

Why is my fixed photo labelled as edited?
Because it is: it combines several moments into one. We think the people who see your photo should be able to tell. The label says it's a composite of your shots and how many eye and mouth regions were taken from other shots. It doesn't contain your name, your location or the other photos.

Can I remove the label?
The app doesn't offer that. Note that some apps and websites strip metadata when you share, so the metadata label and Content Credentials may not survive everywhere. The invisible watermark survives normal re-saving and cropping, but not resizing or deliberate removal.

Which phones are supported?
Android 8 and newer with Google Play services, and iPhone with iOS 18 and newer.

Why does the Android app need Google Play services?
Android's photo picker on older versions and the face detection model (Google ML Kit) are delivered through Google Play services. The detection still runs on your phone; your photos are not sent to Google.

Can I fix a face that's turned away or covered?
Only if that person looks good in one of your other shots. If they're hidden or turned away in all of them, the app tells you and leaves their face as it is.

Why does a fix sometimes look off?
Big head turns between shots, motion blur or a hand in front of the face make blending harder. Try another shot for that face, or Undo.

How do I clear my history?
On Android, tap the trash icon on a fix under Recent fixes, or clear the app's data. On iPhone, swipe a fix to remove it. Uninstalling the app removes all history. Your saved photos stay in your gallery either way.

Does it work with videos or Live Photos?
Not yet. Open Eyes works with still photos.


## How fixed photos are labelled

Source: https://your-domain.example/labels.html

How fixed photos are labelled

A fixed photo shows a moment that was assembled from several shots. We label it so nobody mistakes it for the untouched original.

What a fix actually is

When you fix a face, Open Eyes takes the eyes or the mouth from another of your shots, lines them up and blends them into your favorite. Every pixel was captured by your camera. On-device face detection only finds where the eyes and mouth are; nothing is drawn, invented or generated by AI.

That makes the result a composite capture: a photo combined from several real shots of the same scene. That's the term the photo industry's standard (IPTC) uses, and it's the one we use.

The three labels

LabelWhere it livesWhat it says

IPTC metadataInside the photo file (XMP)Digital source type "composite capture" and a short description of how many eye and mouth regions came from other shots.
Content Credentials (C2PA)A signed record inside the photo file, where your phone supports itThe same facts, signed so that changes to the file can be detected. Includes the app name and version.
Invisible watermarkIn the pixels themselvesThat the photo was edited by Open Eyes, and an edit number. It survives JPEG re-saving and cropping, even when metadata is stripped.

The labels never contain your name, your location, the other shots or anything about the people in the photo.

When a photo isn't labelled

If you save without changing any face, the copy is identical in content to your favorite shot, so it isn't labelled. The Saved screen tells you which labels were added.

Checking a photo

Content Credentials can be inspected with the free Content Credentials Verify tool, and the IPTC fields are shown by most photo managers that read XMP metadata.

Limits
- Many messaging apps and social networks remove metadata when you share, which removes the IPTC label and Content Credentials.
- The watermark doesn't survive resizing, rotation, heavy filters or deliberate removal. It's a helpful hint, not tamper-proof evidence.
- Content Credentials need a recent phone. Where they can't be added, the other two labels still are.


## Privacy

Open Eyes processes photos only on the phone and uploads nothing. See https://your-domain.example/privacy.html
